marchPerKm.note: Infantry and guns moving in formation over open ground. Fatigue runs from 0 (fresh) to 1 (spent). A kilometre's advance costs little; an afternoon of manoeuvre adds up.

gallopPerKm.note: Cavalry at the gallop: a 200 m charge costs 0.12, so a squadron has perhaps four or five good charges in it.

roughFactor.note: Movement on a slope or through a wood or farm costs this much more.

perVolley.note: Loading and firing. Sixty rounds cost about a quarter of a unit's endurance.

meleePerSecond.note: Hand-to-hand fighting exhausts men within minutes.

restPerSecond.note: Recovered while halted, not in melee and not firing: about 0.25 in ten minutes.

restAfterFire.note: A unit that has fired within this time is not resting.

speedLoss.note: Speed is multiplied by 1 - this x fatigue.

reloadSlowdown.note: Reload time is multiplied by 1 + this x fatigue.

meleeLoss.note: Melee power is multiplied by 1 - this x fatigue.

recoveryLoss.note: Morale recovery is multiplied by 1 - this x fatigue.

shockGain.note: Morale lost per casualty is multiplied by 1 + this x fatigue: tired men break sooner.

noChargeAbove.note: Cavalry more tired than this cannot raise a gallop.
